title: Quartet songs and singing for the school principal
summary: Repertoire, parent-teacher meeting and the principal's request, winning the cake.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: What was in your repertoire of songs? When you sang?

Well we used to do all those spiritual songs, but then a couple of them, like one time we sang for, at our school, you know, they had a parent teacher meeting. And we sung for them, you know. And people really applauded, you know. What song? Well they had one particular song, called It Kicked Him Out of Heaven, talking about the devil, you know. And we, Our God, Thee, and all this, you know. All the spiritual songs, you know. Anything else?

Well anyway, I can't really think, you know. But anyway, we sang for the parent teacher meeting, and everybody enjoyed it. And so the next day when I went to school, you see we were all in the same school, but we were in different classes, you know. So a girl came in and said, Mr. Honey, Mr. Honey was the principal, you know. I said, Mr. Honey want to see Curtis Mitchell, you know. Well I know I had did nothing wrong, you know. I'm wondering what he wants. He wants me in his office. So when I go there, I see my brother Ulyss, he's there. And my brother Emile, he's there. And he tell us, he said, look, see I want you all to go in there and do, we're going to go in the bar of Charlie, I want you all to sing them songs that you all sung at the parent teacher meeting. So we told him, well Mr. Honey, see we can go in the bar of Charlie, but my sister can't go in there. She's a girl, you know. So he got some guy out another quartet that sings lead and he had us in the bar of Charlie singing for him, you know.
Were a lot of your peer groups, people your own age, were they singing quartets, singing in church?

Well they had about two, three quartets around our age up there, but they didn't compare with us, you know. Because one time we sang for a church and the woman had baked the cake for the best quartet, you know. But what happened, they called us a fish, you know. And so by the time they got to the, them other guys who were that singing, man, when they called them up, they wasn't there, they done snucked on out of the church, you know. So we got the cake, you know.
